cardiofusion.dataset: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (5 AAMI classes), ECG-signal modality
cardiofusion.loss_weighting: learned homoscedastic uncertainty (Kendall et al., CVPR 2018)
cardiofusion.multimodal_note: Single-modality training. Joint 4-modality fusion + contrastive alignment NOT trained — requires same-patient paired data absent from public benchmarks.

pcg.dataset: CirCor DigiScope (PhysioNet), 942 subjects; 2057 train / 480 val / 626 test recordings
pcg.evaluation: held-out TEST set only (no train-set eval)
pcg.leakage_fix_verified: Loader reported 942 subjects (the contaminated run counted 962), and zero recordings were skipped for a missing metadata row - all 3163 .wav files reconciled to a real subject, so the 20 phantom ids are gone rather than merely excluded.
pcg.selection_caveat: Validation macro-F1 is unstable across epochs (0.159, 0.554, 0.115, 0.454, 0.367, 0.448, 0.367, 0.546); early stopping selected the epoch-2 checkpoint from that noisy curve. Val 0.5539 vs test 0.5347 shows no val overfit, so the figure is honest, but a single run is not a reliable point estimate - quote test_present_vs_absent_auc as the steadier headline and do not present macro-F1 as precise. Repeated runs or subject-level cross-validation are needed for a defensible interval.
pcg.class_note: 'Unknown' is a real CirCor annotation meaning auscultation was inconclusive, not a missing-data marker. Its F1 stays low (0.2651) because the class is genuinely hard and rare, not because of the id-parsing defect - that defect is fixed and no longer feeds this class.
pcg.benchmark_note: Oliveira et al. CirCor JBHI 2022 report ~0.79 weighted murmur accuracy; this genuine run is reported without claiming that value.

withdrawn_previous_result.reason: PATIENT LEAKAGE. heart_sound_loader parsed the subject id with base.rsplit('_', 1), which splits CirCor repeat-recording names on the LAST underscore: '50204_MV_1.wav' yielded patient_id '50204_MV' instead of '50204'. Effects: (1) 20 phantom patients (962 counted vs 942 real), (2) those ids missed the metadata table so their murmur label silently defaulted to the 'Unknown' CLASS - conflating 'no metadata row' with the real annotation meaning 'auscultation inconclusive', which is why Unknown F1 was worst at 0.269, and (3) the subject-level split treated '50204_MV' and '50204' as different people, so one patient's recordings could appear in BOTH train and test.
withdrawn_previous_result.fix: sid now parsed with base.partition('_') (part before the FIRST underscore); recordings with no metadata row are excluded and counted rather than labelled 'Unknown'.
withdrawn_previous_result.outcome: Re-run on 2026-08-01 after the fix. Present-vs-Absent AUC fell 0.7981 -> 0.7611, the direction leakage removal predicts. Accuracy ROSE 0.6438 -> 0.7604 because the 20 phantom ids previously missed the metadata table and were force-labelled 'Unknown'; they now carry their true labels, mostly the majority class 'Absent'.

pcg.data_integrity: RESOLVED 2026-07-31. 85286_AV.wav was truncated (header declared 161280 data bytes, file held 15974) because the first download was killed mid-write and the resume used wget -nc, which skips any file that EXISTS without checking completeness. Repaired by wget -r -N -c, which issued a range request and returned '206 Partial Content ... saved [161324/161324]' - full size, verified by byte count, not assumed. CirCor completeness confirmed: RECORDS 3163 with 3163 each of .hea/.wav/.tsv on disk. Byte-level verification of all 9489 files against the shipped SHA256SUMS.txt remains optional insurance against a hypothetical second corrupt file.

vfdb.dataset: MIT-BIH VFDB (PhysioNet), 22 recordings, 5s windows; 6285 train / 1257 val / 1676 test segments
vfdb.evaluation: held-out TEST set only (no train-set eval, no random weights)
vfdb.class_note: Non-targeted rhythms (AFIB, SBR, etc.) grouped into the Normal/background class; the binary head is the safety-relevant output.

withdrawn_previous_result.reason: NOT REPORTABLE - artifact of a single-class dataset, not a model result. core/vfdb_loader.read_atr fell back to a hand-rolled WFDB byte parser (wfdb.rdann raised OverflowError under NumPy 2) whose SKIP handling byte-swapped the 32-bit interval, producing annotation offsets up to 1.99e10 on a 525000-sample signal. Every window therefore fell before the first valid annotation and was labelled Normal: 0 dangerous segments in train/val/test. Accuracy 1.0 and rhythm_f1 1.0 were the trivial single-class solution; F1(dangerous) 0.0 and AUC NaN show the detector never fired.
withdrawn_previous_result.fix: wfdb upgraded to 4.3.1 (pandas 2.2.3); read_atr now uses wfdb.rdann and reports parse failures instead of silently falling back; train_vfdb raises if any split is single-class.

vfdb.small_n_caveat: 22 recordings. The 15/3/4 single split (test F1(dang) 0.5147 / AUC 0.8046 vs val F1 0.894 / AUC 0.984) is one draw and is NOT the headline - see cross_validation. Its low value was an unlucky 4-recording test fold, not leakage: 2x5-fold recording-level CV puts 9 of 10 folds at AUC 0.913-0.983 and the single split val AUC 0.984 already matched that bulk. Genuine downside variance remains (one fold at AUC 0.6414 / F1 0.3881).
vfdb.rhythm_head_caveat: 4-class macro-F1 is underpowered - ASYS/HGEA/VER are rare. CV mean 0.4512 [0.3831, 0.5193]. Do NOT quote the rhythm head as a strength; the binary Dangerous-vs-Normal head is the safety-relevant output.
vfdb.headline: cross_validation (below) is the reportable result; the single-split test_* fields are one draw retained for provenance.

cross_validation.protocol: 2x repeated 5-fold cross-validation, folds are WHOLE RECORDINGS stratified by dangerous-window fraction; validation recordings drawn from the training pool only
cross_validation.evaluation: each test fold scored exactly once, after early stopping on val F1
cross_validation.interval_caveat: The 95% interval is a t-interval over fold scores. Folds share training recordings, so fold scores are not independent and this interval is OPTIMISTIC — it understates true uncertainty. It describes spread across folds, not a confidence interval over patients. With 22 recordings this is a limit of the dataset, not of the resampling scheme.
cross_validation.range_note: Quote the observed_fold_range alongside the interval. The superseded single split scored AUC 0.8046 which lies BELOW this interval low of 0.8466 - a prior recording-level estimate falling outside the interval is direct evidence the t-interval is too narrow, as interval_caveat warns.

heartdisease.dataset: UCI Cleveland Heart Disease (Detrano et al. 1989), Kaggle johnsmith88 mirror
heartdisease.dedup_note: Kaggle file duplicates the 303-record Cleveland cohort; trained on unique rows only.
heartdisease.evaluation: repeated-CV mean±95% CI (headline) + 25% held-out; NO train-set eval
heartdisease.baseline_comparison_note: Logistic and GBT reported on identical folds (reviewer R8): a BERT-MoE must beat plain baselines to justify its complexity.
